a <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-COUNTY">county</a>, forming with Hoya one of the provinces of the <a class="xref" href="../1778/vol6.html#article-KINGDOM">kingdom</a> of <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-HANOVER">Hanover</a>. It extends over 266 <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SQUARE">square</a> miles, <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol0.html#article-OR">or</a> 170,240 acres, and contains 14,200 inhabitants. One <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol0.html#article-PART">part</a> of it, called Auburg, was transferred in 1815 from <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-HESSE">Hesse</a> Cassel. The only industry except <a class="xref" href="vol2.html#article-AGRICULTURE">agriculture</a> is applied to the <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol3.html#article-SPINNING">spinning</a> and <a class="xref" href="vol21.html#article-WEAVING">weaving</a> of <a class="xref" href="vol14.html#article-FLAX">flax</a>. The <a class="xref" href="vol6.html#article-CHIEF">chief</a> <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-PLACE">place</a> of the same name is situated on the river Hunte, and contains 353 houses, with 2068 inhabitants.

DIEPPE

Pages 26-27

an arrondissement of the department of the Lower <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SEINE">Seine</a>, in France. It is 490 <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SQUARE">square</a> miles in <a class="xref" href="vol9.html#article-EXTENT">extent</a>, DIERDORF and contains eight cantons, divided into 292 communes, with a <a class="xref" href="vol18.html#article-POPULATION">population</a> of 104,207 persons. The <a class="xref" href="vol6.html#article-CHIEF">chief</a> <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-PLACE">place</a> is the <a class="xref" href="vol6.html#article-CITY">city</a> of the same name on the Seine, at the mouth of the river <a class="xref" href="../1778/vol1.html#article-ARQUES">Arques</a>. It is fortified on the <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SEA">sea</a> and <a class="xref" href="vol13.html#article-LAND">land</a> sides, and is in the shape of an <a class="xref" href="vol12.html#article-IRREGULAR">irregular</a> triangle, whose longest side is towards the sea. It contains 3000 houses, and about 20,000 inhabitants, chiefly dependent on the <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-COMMERCE">commerce</a> of the port. Being the best inlet for <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-PARIS">Paris</a>, it is the <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-GREAT">great</a> depot for colonial goods, and the <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-RESORT">resort</a> of foreign ships, especially of those from <a class="xref" href="vol2.html#article-AMERICA">America</a>. There are many <a class="xref" href="../1778/vol0.html#article-MANUFACTURES">manufactures</a>, but principally of the kind connected with the equipment of ships; and, besides these, some <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SUGAR">sugar</a> and <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SALT">salt</a> refineries. From this port William the Conqueror sailed with his forces for England. <a class="xref" href="vol13.html#article-LONG">Long</a>. 0° 59', 7' E. Lat. 49° 55' 17' N.

DIETETICS
